from: October book, night 2 (Like a Gentle Shepherd)
p1: Isaiah wrote about how the Lord takes care of His people. He used a picture everyone in his land knew.
Isaiah said, “He shall feed His flock like a shepherd.” A good shepherd finds green grass and cool water for his sheep.
Baby lambs have short, wobbly legs. So the shepherd gathers the lambs in his arms. He carries them close to his heart.
p2: He walks slowly and gently with the mother sheep too. Isaiah was talking about Jesus! Years later, Jesus said, “I am the good shepherd.” He knows each one of His sheep.
You are one of Jesus’s little lambs. When you feel tired or small, He holds you close. Tonight, you can feel safe in His love.
old: Long ago, Heavenly Father's people had stopped listening to Him, and they were taken far, far away from their homes to a land called Babylon. They missed home. They were tired and sad. So Heavenly Father sent a helper named Isaiah. A prophet is someone Heavenly Father tells His words to, so he can tell them to everybody else.

The very first word Isaiah said was a soft one: comfort. Comfort means making a sad heart feel better, the way a hug does. Then Isaiah said a voice would call out, "Make the road smooth! The Lord is coming!" Making the road ready means getting your heart ready for somebody you love. And the Lord is Jesus. Isaiah was talking about Jesus.

Isaiah said Jesus would not come stomping and loud like a king in a parade. He would come like a shepherd, walking slow and gentle. Isaiah said shepherd because his people kept sheep, and every little child there knew exactly what a good shepherd does all day.

A shepherd takes care of sheep. When a lamb, a baby sheep, gets too tired to walk, the shepherd scoops it up and holds it close to his heart. And he walks extra slow for the mama sheep, so nobody gets left behind. Isaiah said Jesus is like that shepherd, and that is why Heavenly Father sent that message to His tired people: so they would know they were not left behind.

You are one of His little lambs. When you are tired, or sad, or your tower falls down, Jesus holds you close. And you can be a comforter too. Tonight, when someone near you is sad, you can do the soft thing first, like Isaiah's soft first word.
